[approach_variants] The first-ascent party rappelled from the col into the bergschrund and climbed a 15 ft vertical ice wall to get out of it onto the Boston Glacier.
[approach_variants] Expect the schrund to be the awkward part of the day before the climbing starts.

name: Northwest Face
text: [seasonal_hazards] Cold, shaded northwest aspect holding snow and ice well into summer..
[seasonal_hazards] Rockfall/icefall and mixed-terrain route-finding on a big face;
[seasonal_hazards] a fall or being caught by rockfall/icefall on the shaded aspect carries serious consequence..
[seasonal_hazards] Approach crosses the Boston and/or Forbidden glaciers;
[seasonal_hazards] crevasse hazard is present and increases through the season as bridges deteriorate.
[approach_variants] All the way round to the Forbidden Glacier's north arm.

[approach_variants] The recorded approach goes the long way round: from the Boston Basin trailhead, three to four miles by the old mine road and the climbers' path with four stream crossings to high camp near 6,400 ft, often pushing on to a bench near 7,500 ft beside the Quien Sa

[approach_variants] Ascend the west side of the Quien Sabe to the notch above Sharkfin Col, rappel onto the Boston Glacier below the bergschrund, traverse that heavily crevassed glacier, and continue around to the north arm of the Forbidden Glacier on the mountain's other side.

[approach_variants] Other parties reach the same basin without the Boston Glacier at all — by dropping west off the North Ridge line, by rappelling from the West Ridge notch over crevasses and moats, or over Torment Col.
[approach_variants] From the north arm, about 900 ft of 30 to 40-plus degree snow and ice leads to the base of the rock..
[approach_variants] Two crevassed glaciers before any climbing, with a large crevasse that opens around 7,600 ft in many seasons and can cost real time.
[approach_variants] A moat or bergschrund where the snow pulls back from the foot of the rib.
[approach_variants] A shaded, cold aspect that holds hard ice late, and a face that tops out at a cornice near 8,375 ft.
[approach_variants] The deciding fact is which glacier you are standing on, and it settles this route against both its neighbours in one look.

name: West Ridge
text: [seasonal_hazards] The approach crosses the remnant glacier below the south face, with a lower and an upper bergschrund at the foot of the couloir.
[seasonal_hazards] Late season these open into deep moats and slots down to rock;
[seasonal_hazards] rope up while the glacier is snow-covered or crevassed.
[approach_variants] From the Boston Basin high camp, traverse up and east across talus and the remains of the Quien Sabe Glacier toward Forbidden's south face.
[approach_variants] Where the glacier is melted out, a class 3 rock spur on climber's right is usually faster and drier than staying on snow;
[approach_variants] where it is snow-covered or crevassed, rope up.
[approach_variants] The couloir itself runs about 500 ft and steepens to 40–50° near the top, which is where crampons and an axe stop being optional.
[approach_variants] Jun–early Aug, while it still holds snow.
[approach_variants] A moat where the snow pulls back from the rock guards the top of the couloir.
[approach_variants] 40–50° snow near the top, on ground where a slip does not stop on its own..

[approach_variants] The notch is the gap in the crest at the foot of the West Ridge proper, and the couloir below it is the obvious continuous snow line splitting the left-hand edge of the south face.
[approach_variants] Navigate to the notch, not to the first gully you reach — several lines start off the same snowfield and only this one tops out at the crest.
[approach_variants] When the couloir has gone to loose talus and scree, the usual line moves off the snow onto the rock gully system immediately west — climber's left — of it.
[approach_variants] Late summer, once the couloir has gone icy, rocky and prone to rockfall, and the rock gullies to its west offer a surer way to the notch without a snow-to-rock transition..

name: East Ridge
